result:
I woke up this morning to the sound of the neighbor's dog learning a new trick. Not barking, just a soft, confused whine every time it hears the doorbell and doesn't get to go out. It's 7:14 a.m. and the light is that particular pale gold that makes everything look like it's been left out to air dry.

I made coffee in the chipped blue mug that says WORLD'S OKAYEST COUSIN. It was a gift from my sister in 2019, and I have never corrected her. It is a good mug. The coffee is too hot for the first three sips, which I drink anyway because I'm impatient and also because I like the small punishment.

There's a spider in the corner of the kitchen window. It has been there for weeks, rebuilding its web every night after I absentmindedly wipe it away with my sleeve. Today it has caught a moth. The moth is still moving. The spider is very still. I watch them for a minute longer than is polite.

I think about how many small negotiations happen in a house when no one is really paying attention. The fridge hums, the pipes tick, the dog next door sighs. The web holds. The coffee cools.

On my walk later I passed the laundromat and the old man who always reads the newspaper out loud to himself on the bench. He was on the sports page today and he laughed at something. A real, sudden laugh, like he was surprised by his own joke.

I don't know why I remember these things. Maybe because they don't ask for anything. No one is asking me to remember the spider or the dog or the man laughing. They just happened, and then they were gone, and the day kept moving.

Sometimes I wish I could file my thoughts the way I file socks. Pairs together, clean and easy to find. But most days my mind is more like a kitchen counter after breakfast. A few crumbs, a damp towel, a pen, a thought about whether I should text someone back, a half-remembered song lyric.

And yet, I like it. I like the clutter. I like that there is a spider in the window who doesn't know she's part of my morning.

I'm going to go water the plants now. One of them is definitely dying, but I love it anyway.
